articles.summary: The Auto-Router now reads the assistant's own recent tool calls, notices when an agentic task is stuck in a retry loop, and escalates it one tier automatically, the same bump escalation_keywords already offers.
articles.title: Auto-Router: Escalate a Task That Gets Stuck

articles.summary: Day 0 support for Meta Muse Spark 1.3 on LiteLLM, with cost tracking for both the standard and contributor tiers.
articles.title: Day 0 support: Meta Muse Spark 1.3

articles.summary: Harness-aware Auto-Router updates for Claude Code and Codex: less classifier context, encrypted task support, and clearer routing logs.
articles.title: Auto-Router Updates: Harness-Aware Routing

articles.summary: How LiteLLM preserves caller identity across shared agents, governs model and MCP access, and enforces independent budgets for each business unit.
articles.title: Secure shared AI agents with identity-aware access and spend controls

articles.summary: The Auto-Router now supports more routing configurations: context-window escalation moves oversized prompts to the cheapest tier that fits them before dispatch, modality routing sends image requests to tiers that can see, classification can run on user turns only, and shadow evaluations can compare several router configs on a team's live traffic.
articles.title: Auto-Router: Route on Context Size and Modality

articles.summary: Tune AutoRouter heuristic dimensions for specific workloads, improve classification accuracy, and configure tiers from models you already serve.
articles.title: AutoRouter: Tune Heuristics for Your Traffic

articles.summary: Day 0 support for Claude Fable 5.1 on the LiteLLM AI Gateway, with the 0.025x cache read price tracked from the first call.
articles.title: Day 0 Support: Claude Fable 5.1

articles.summary: Running three models on the same task and synthesizing their work solved 14 of 21 Terminal-Bench tasks against 9 for Claude Fable-5 alone. Total spend rose 36%, cost per solved task fell 12%, and turn latency went up 5x.
articles.title: Introducing LiteLLM Fusion: 56% More Tasks Solved Than Fable 5

articles.summary: The complexity router's LLM classifier can now use different compression than the model call it routes to. The classifier only needs enough context to route correctly, not to generate an answer. In internal testing, compressing it aggressively cut classification costs a further 32% beyond shared compression, with no change in routing accuracy.
articles.title: AutoRouter Per-Hop Compression: Cut LLM Classifier Costs Another 32%

articles.summary: day 0 support for Gemini 3.8 Flash on LiteLLM, with launch pricing tracked across Google AI Studio and Vertex AI.
articles.title: Day 0 support: Gemini 3.8 Flash

articles.summary: Heuristic v2 is a new classifier for LiteLLM's AutoRouter, pretrained across multiple rounds of graded response data so it ships with zero cold start. On a 21-task Terminal-Bench 2.0 subset it solved 3 more tasks than Heuristic v1, at 45% lower cost per solved task and lower latency.
articles.title: Introducing AutoRouter Heuristic v2: 27% More Tasks Solved at 45% Lower Cost

articles.summary: Routing each agent turn by what the agent is doing, exploring, implementing, or verifying, instead of by how hard the prompt looks. On a SWE-bench Verified subset it matched fixed Claude Opus-5 quality for 46% less, with 86% of turns never touching a frontier model.
articles.title: Subtask-Specific Routing: Same Quality, 46% Less Cost

articles.summary: LiteLLM's updated SOC 2 Type 2 report is now available through the LiteLLM Trust Center.
articles.title: Our Updated SOC 2 Type 2 Report Is Available

articles.summary: Day 0 support for OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on LiteLLM, with pricing, reasoning params, and the Responses API bridge.
articles.title: Day 0 Support: GPT-6 Astra
